Independent exact witness arithmetic and primality checks
correctness.rationale: The diagonal pair is impossible since g(a)≡1 (mod a). For a hypothetical pair with 2≤a<b, set z=g(a)/b. Then 1≤z<a by g(a)<a² and b>a; bz≡1 (mod a) gives z²g(b)≡g(z) (mod a). Thus a|g(z) and z|g(a), without any cancellation or assumed coprimality. The case z=1 implies a|1; otherwise the pair (z,a) contradicts minimal maximum. Grouping by gcd gives ∑_{d|n}φ(n/d)/d and, on squarefree n, the quotient ∏g(p)/n. If this is integral, each prime p divides some other support prime's g-value. In the Finding's convention, choosing one such destination at each vertex forces a cycle, necessarily of length at least three. Independent exact trial division through 18, 348 and 3116 confirmed the three witness primes. The exact checks g(349)=121453, g(121453)=1519×9710803, and g(9710803)=270199671043×349 give the witness and the asserted quotient on multiplying. The Assumptions paragraph and checker use arrows opposite to the Finding; with the Finding's convention the cycle is 349→9710803→121453→349. All stated existence/nonexistence claims are invariant under reversing all arrows, so the orientation inconsistency is editorial, not a failure of the theorem.
residual_risks: The finite check through a=5000 in the frozen package was not replayed; it is not needed for the descent proof. No nonsquarefree version or witness minimality claim is certified by the frozen proof.

originality.rationale: A distinct co-dated catalogue entry explicitly states and proves the same all-integer mutual-divisibility lemma by the same strict descent, supplies the same three-prime witness and exact value, and establishes a stronger least-witness claim. Its Euler-product criterion plus that lemma already forces the squarefree support bound: one prime would need a loop and two would need a mutual pair. The coverage is affirmative and is independent of resolving same-day priority.
residual_risks: Bounded source comparison; does not decide historical priority. The failure rests on exact mathematical coverage by a different record, not on the existence of a later generalization or on a short database lookup.

value.rationale: An all-integer structural obstruction making a natural arithmetic bound sharp would be valuable on its own. Here the precise obstruction is already given and used in the same arithmetic setting with the identical witness. The only remaining difference, stating the one- and two-prime exclusions as a support bound, is a direct consequence of the covered loop/pair obstruction and Euler product. Neither a new extremal fact nor a new independent arithmetic application survives in this package.
residual_risks: The scientific utility of the common lemma and its motivating problem is not in question; no separate repair of this frozen claim was established.
